headline.text: MV Arctic Fern (V007, VG-1088) is the one vessel already projected to miss its Rotterdam berth window. Its revised ETA is 23 hours after the window closes. MV Kestrel Bay (V008) and MV Celtic Dawn (V012) come next. Each has an unverified engine-fault report but no recorded delay.

interpretation.text: "Next week" is Mon 2026-11-02 to Sun 2026-11-08, using Rotterdam port-local dates. Voyages are selected by revised ETA. Berth-window arithmetic uses UTC.

confirmed_facts.text: Arctic Fern (SGSIN to NLRTM) has status Delayed with a recorded delay of 33 h. Its ETA moved from 2026-11-03T05:00Z to 2026-11-04T14:00Z. Its berth window is 2026-11-03T03:00Z to 15:00Z, so the revised ETA falls after the window closes.
Confirmed incident INC-221 (hull fouling / speed loss), reported by the technical manager, has an attributed delay of 33 h. This matches the recorded delay in full.

The other five arrivals show a revised ETA 10 h before their window closes and a recorded delay of 0: Northern Lark (VG-1097), Kestrel Bay (VG-1091), Amber Coast (VG-1099), Celtic Dawn (VG-1102) and Rio Verde (VG-1095). Rio Verde has not yet departed; its status is Scheduled.

unverified_reports.text: Kestrel Bay (V008, VG-1091) has a Reported auxiliary engine fault, INC-224, from a crew message sent 2026-10-24. Its attributed delay is null (unknown), and the three crew facts about it are unverified.
Celtic Dawn (V012, VG-1102) has a Reported main engine fuel pump fault, INC-219, from the master's report of 2026-10-19. Its attributed delay is null (unknown).

inferences.text: Arctic Fern is the most likely to miss its window. The ETA already slips past the window by 23 h, and the cause is a confirmed hull-fouling speed loss. The window would only be met if the ETA were recovered by more than 23 h, which seems unlikely given the 33 h slip. Even a recovered ETA would still face the port's waiting times.
inferences.based_on: Vessel-specific voyage record and confirmed incident. This is a projection that depends on the ETA.

inferences.text: Kestrel Bay and Celtic Dawn are the next most at risk. Each has an unverified engine fault, and their ETAs have 10 h of margin with no slip recorded yet. A fault that costs more than 10 h would push either vessel past its window. Their risk is speculative until the faults are verified.
inferences.based_on: Unverified incident reports plus the ETA margin. Berth windows are 12 h wide, so a 10 h margin is not large.

inferences.text: Port-wide context raises the risk for every arrival. Rotterdam congestion was High on each day from 19 to 26 Oct, with average waits of 28 to 40 h and 25 vessels at anchor on 26 Oct. If this persists, even on-time vessels could wait past their windows. This is port-wide and not a fact about any one vessel.
inferences.based_on: Port-wide congestion feed through 2026-10-26. It is not forecast data.

data_gaps.text: Congestion data ends 2026-10-26, so conditions for 2 to 8 Nov are unknown, not normal.
The messages/extra folder (45 files) was not loaded, so further reports on these vessels may be missing.
Rio Verde has not yet sailed from BRSSZ, and I did not check conditions at its origin.

recommended_checks.text: Ask the Arctic Fern technical manager (Nordwave Marine) for a recovery speed plan. Also ask Rotterdam for a new berth slot after 2026-11-04T14:00Z.
